question: Across species that are prospectively balanced for within-cell replication, does flower-colour composition diverge with geographic separation within species?
claim_role: new prospective follow-up; cannot rescue or rewrite H1-H6b

species_discovery.rule: species must have at least 2 metadata-only candidate observations in each of at least 6 frozen 18x9 H1 cells

target_cells.eligible_cells: only species cells with at least 2 observations in the old metadata-only discovery pool
target_cells.selection: deterministic maximin spread on H1 cell centroids: first choose the cell with greatest mean distance to all eligible cells, then repeatedly choose the cell maximizing minimum distance to already selected cells; ties use lower cell_id

fresh_metadata_acquisition.target_queries: one query for each frozen species x target cell
fresh_metadata_acquisition.retention_tie_break: stable SHA256 of protocol seed, species taxon id, cell id and observation id

premeasurement_gate.per_species_requirement: at least 5 of 6 target cells retain exactly 30 fresh candidate photos after exclusions and observer cap

measurement.method: location-blind ROI-v4 flower localization plus the fixed species-independent sRGB-to-CIELAB reference palette used by the completed random photo-first atlas
measurement.mixed_uncertain: structural measurement missingness, never a biological fifth state

final_evaluability.monomorphic_or_zero_colour_distance_spec: retain and define species-level rho as 0 rather than exclude
final_evaluability.reason: Do not condition inclusion on observed colour variation.

primary_statistic.cell_colour: mean soft four-state colour composition within each species x target cell
primary_statistic.pairwise_geographic_distance: great-circle distance between frozen H1 cell centroids
primary_statistic.species_level: Spearman rho between pairwise geographic distance and pairwise colour JSD; predeclare rho=0 when colour JSD has zero variance
primary_statistic.global_information_weighted: mean species-level rho weighted by number of evaluable cell pairs

null.operation: within each species, permute individual classifiable photo soft four-state colour vectors across its retained photo rows while keeping target-cell assignments and exact classifiable photo counts per cell fixed; recompute cell compositions, pairwise JSD, species rhos and both global statistics
preserves: exact classifiable photo count per species x cell

support_requires_all: observed equal-species mean rho > 0 with one-sided permutation p < 0.05
observed pair-count-weighted mean rho > 0 with one-sided permutation p < 0.05

claim_ceiling: A supported H7 would show that, in an independently resampled and prospectively balanced multi-species frame, flower-colour composition tends to diverge with geographic separation within species. It would not show a shared global boundary, identify a climate or pollinator driver, or establish adaptation, selection or pigment mechanism.
